title: Operational Steadfastness — Cross-Functional Plan for SLOs & Reliability
summary: A compact, tactical plan to coordinate engineering, product, SRE, and support for defining, instrumenting, and rolling out service-level objectives (SLOs) across priority services. Focused on two sprint cycles and a lightweight steady-state cadence.
body:
Purpose:
To create a focused, cross-functional execution plan that moves a select set of services from concept SLOs to production guarded SLOs, with clear telemetry, playbooks, and rollout controls.

Context and constraints:
- Multiple teams have ad-hoc SLO proposals; we need a single pragmatic pipeline to avoid fragmentation.
- Telemetry gaps (cold paths, sampling variance) exist for several endpoints.
- Customer-impact sensitivity: some services (embeddings, streaming) require tighter latencies and bespoke runbooks.
- Limited SRE headcount for initial rollout — prioritize highest-customer-impact services.

Scope (MVP):
- Define and agree SLI definitions for 5 priority services (API generation, chat routing, embeddings, KV-cache, model-routing).
- Implement missing telemetry for those SLIs with end-to-end tests.
- Draft runbooks and automated alerting thresholds for error budget and latency breaches.
- Execute canary rollouts with rollback gates and a 2-week steady-state review.

Objectives (success criteria):
- 5 services have production-grade SLIs and dashboards.
- Alerts for SLO burn hit fewer false positives than 30% during the initial 2-week window.
- One fully exercised incident response drill per service before wide rollout.
- Clear ownership and onboarding checklist completed for each service.

Stakeholders and roles (high level):
- Product (service PM): define customer-facing availability expectations and priority.
- SRE (lead): SLO design reviews, rollout gates, incident exercises.
- Backend engineers: implement instrumentation and remediation code.
- Observability: dashboarding, sampling guidance, metric catalog updates.
- Support/CS: runbook feedback loop and customer comms templates.

Workstreams (parallel, 4-week cadence suggested):
1) SLO Definition & Acceptance
   - Kickoff workshop (1 day) to align on user journeys and error definitions.
   - Output: SLO proposal doc per service (SLO, SLI, measurement window, alert policy).
   - Owner: Product + SRE.

2) Metrics & Instrumentation
   - Inventory current telemetry; spike work for missing traces/KPIs (prometheus exporters, traces, logs).
   - Instrument end-to-end latency and correctness checks (synthetic tests).
   - Output: metrics merged, metric catalog entries updated, dashboard mockups.
   - Owner: Backend + Observability.

3) Alerting & Runbooks
   - Convert SLO thresholds into concrete alert rules and escalation pages.
   - Draft runbooks with play-by-play (detection, mitigation, rollback, postmortem checklist).
   - Run a tabletop for each runbook.
   - Owner: SRE + Support.

4) Canary Rollouts & Safety Gates
   - Define canary traffic % and health checks.
   - Implement automated rollback hooks and a canary dashboard.
   - Run 48–72h canary, then 14-day steady-state review with burn analysis.
   - Owner: Backend + Release Eng.

5) Postmortem & Feedback Loop
   - Structured postmortem template focusing on SLO drift and telemetry gaps.
   - Feed improvements back into instrumentation and team onboarding.
   - Owner: SRE + Product.

Practical runbook checklist (template):
- Trigger definition (metric, window)
- Initial triage steps (who, how to verify)
- Short-term mitigations (circuit-breakers, routing to safe model variants)
- Rollback steps and verification post-rollback
- Customer comms draft and responsible contact
- Postmortem owner and 72h follow-up actions

Minimum viable telemetry spec (for each SLI):
- Unique metric name (dot-delimited), unit, aggregation (p50/p95/p99), cardinality guidance
- Instrumentation library + example call site
- Synthetic test spec (payload, expected output, threshold)

Timeline and sprint map (example two sprint plan):
- Week 0 (Prep): Stakeholder kickoff, priority service list finalized, workshop scheduled.
- Sprint A (Weeks 1–2): SLO proposals created; instrumentation spikes for top 3 services; dashboards prototyped.
- Sprint B (Weeks 3–4): Alerts & runbooks drafted; canary infra wired up; first canaries launched for 2 services.
- Weeks 5–6: 14-day steady-state review starts for canaries; incident drills completed.
- Week 7: Postmortems, finalize rollouts, handoff to steady-state cadence.

Milestones and acceptance (explicit gates):
- Milestone 1 (SLO sign-off): All SLO proposal docs approved by Product + SRE.
- Gate A (Telemetry complete): End-to-end synthetic checks in CI for listed SLIs.
- Gate B (Runbooks & Alerts): Runbooks published and table-toped; alert false-positive rate measured in canary.
- Gate C (Canary safe): No major customer-impacting incidents and error-budget burn within thresholds during steady-state.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Underinstrumentation leads to blind spots. Mitigation: Conservative rollout, synthetic checks first.
- Risk: Alert fatigue. Mitigation: Two-tier alerting (pageable vs. non-pageable) and tuned debounce windows.
- Risk: Cross-team triage friction. Mitigation: RACI on each runbook + monthly triage rotas.

Communications plan:
- Weekly 15m sync (ops standup) between SRE, product, and backend leads during active rollout.
- Shared channel #ops-steadfastness for real-time updates, with automated canary status posts.
- Biweekly stakeholder summary email (SRE lead -> exec and product).

Operational steady-state (post-rollout):
- Monthly SLO review (owner reports burn, changes to SLO or instrumentation).
- Quarterly SLO audit (sampling, cardinality, cost vs. signal tradeoffs).
- Oncall pairing: rotate a feature engineer into the SRE rota during first 90 days post rollout.

Next immediate actions (first 7 days):
- Schedule kickoff workshop and invite list assembled (owner: Marina).
- PMs to submit SLO one-pagers for priority services.
- Observability to run a telemetry dry-run and list 3 high-risk measurement gaps.
- Release eng to prepare canary template repo and one-click dashboard.

Appendix: quick templates (copy-paste friendly)
- SLO one-pager header: service, user journey, SLI def, threshold, measurement window, owner, rollback criteria.
- Tabletop script outline: scenario, detection, mitigation run, escalation, postmortem triggers.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic — we trade absolute completeness for rapid, repeatable rollout patterns.
- Please flag any service that cannot accept synthetic testing or has regulatory telemetry constraints.
